bibliographic.title: A chatbot for mental health support: exploring the impact of Emohaa on reducing mental distress in China
bibliographic.authors: Sahand Sabour, Wen Zhang, Xiyao Xiao, Yuwei Zhang, Yinhe Zheng, Jiaxin Wen, Jialu Zhao, Minlie Huang
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sabour, S., Zhang, W., Xiao, X., Zhang, Y., Zheng, Y., Wen, J., Zhao, J., & Huang, M. (2023). A chatbot for mental health support: Exploring the impact of Emohaa on reducing mental distress in China. Frontiers in Digital Health, 5, 1133987. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2023.1133987

methodology.study_design: RCT with three arms (Emohaa CBT-Bot, Emohaa Full, control); intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses
methodology.sample_description: Participants randomly assigned to use Emohaa variants or control in a mental health support study in China
methodology.technology_context: Emohaa conversational agent with template-based CBT-Bot and generative dialogue ES-Bot for emotional support; deep learning and NLP referenced

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Primary contribution is an RCT evaluating clinical effectiveness of a mental health chatbot; provided text does not address conversational governance, LLM governance mechanisms, accountability, oversight, audit, compliance, guardrails, or related operational controls.
eligibility.decision_rationale: The article clearly fits conversational AI in a regulated healthcare domain, but its central aim is symptom reduction efficacy rather than governance of conversational or generative systems. Technology is described as conversational agents using NLP, deep learning, and a generative dialogue platform, without explicit LLM-specific governance content in the supplied text.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on the excerpted text. The study appears methodologically appropriate for an efficacy RCT, but transparency on ethics, limitations, and full data-collection procedures cannot be fully judged from the provided pages.

cerqual.explanation: For the review question on conversational governance in LLM-based regulated systems, relevance is low because the supplied text centers on mental distress outcomes, not governance. Within its own efficacy aim, coherence and reported RCT design appear adequate, but only partial text was available for full methodological appraisal.

coding.theme: Clinical effectiveness of conversational mental health support
coding.subtheme: CBT and emotional support chatbot RCT in China

synthesis.main_claim: Emohaa, a conversational agent providing CBT-based cognitive support and emotional venting support, significantly reduced mental distress symptoms compared with control in an RCT.
synthesis.contribution: Empirical evidence that a Chinese-language mental health conversational agent combining template-based CBT exercises and generative emotional support can improve depression, negative affect, and insomnia outcomes.
synthesis.use_in_review: Low value as central evidence for conversational governance; may serve only as peripheral contextual background on conversational agents in regulated mental healthcare if broader background is needed.
